desk.headline: Revenue up 55% to $1.47bn, beat; 2026 revenue and EBITDA outlook raised
results: Revenue rose 55% to $1.47bn, about 6% above the analysts' estimate; rental revenue grew 49% on a 32% bigger fleet.
Equipment sales jumped 76% to $294m, mostly sales into its OWN programme, where outside investors own fleet the company rents out.
Rental segment adjusted EBITDA rose 52% to $491m and the margin widened to 44.1%; older (mature) branches earned 54% over 12 months.
Net income was $20m ($0.03 a share); excluding $26m of founders' share awards, adjusted EPS was $0.16.
Opened 18 locations (448 in total); operating cash flow was -$179m for nine months, and net leverage eased to 3.4x.

guidance.summary: Compared with the August release, the 2026 revenue range rose to $5.81–6.05bn and adjusted core EBITDA to $2.14–2.22bn; on the call management said these levels were first set in October. The CEO said he sees a chance to beat the outlook.

points: About $900m of equipment went on rent for the first time in Q3, versus about $550m a year earlier; demand is strongest on mega-projects.
Fuel, delivery, re-rent and service costs took about 3.1 points off margins, more than offset by overhead savings; re-rent is seen as temporary.
Q4 rental revenue and rental EBITDA growth is expected in the mid-40s %, with Q4 free cash flow of about $400m.
Net leverage is targeted at low 3x by end-2026; management can move from growth to "harvest mode" if the economy weakens.
No 2027 guidance yet; data centres are about 10% of revenue and more 2027 detail is due with Q1 results.
call.source: Q3 2026 call transcript — Earnings Whispers, 10 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (12 Aug 2026)

watch: Whether Q4 delivers the roughly $400m of free cash flow promised after negative operating cash flow so far this year.
Margin drag from fuel, delivery and re-rent costs as the fleet grows.
The first 2027 outlook, due early next year.
